title: Dual-aspect monism: mind and body are two appearances of one function

statements.text: Body and mind are two appearances, first-person and third-person, of one underlying thing. What that thing is made of is a function, abstracted from both manifestations, as memory is abstracted from remembering and from the neuronal assembly that holds the memory. Laws stated at that depth, ideally in mathematics, explain both appearances and leave no explanatory gap.

sources.quote: This is the dual-apect monist position on the mind/body problem
Memory is not a stuff; it is a function.
biological explanations (as opposed to descriptions) are best formulated in neither interoceptive nor exteroceptive phenomenal terms, but rather as abstractions
